newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-Poland moves ahead with banking mergers.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Poland moves ahead with banking mergers.

text.p: Poland moved ahead on Tuesday with a recently-approved bank merger plan by transferring treasury stakes in several banks to others that have been picked to form larger banking groups.

The finance ministry, which represents the state treasury, moved its 32.9 percent stake in the listed Polish Development Bank SA (PBR) to the larger state-owned Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA to boost capital ahead of its privatisation in early 1997.

The ministry also more than tripled the capital of the state-owned Polska Kasa Opieki SA (Pekao) bank with a new stock issue with the aid of the shares the treasury owns in three state-owned banks that Pekao will take over.
Pekao is to lead a banking group that will also comprise mid-sized regional banks Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA, Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA and Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA.

Commenting on the PBK deal, the finance ministry, which has cut its stake in PBR to 29.54 percent from 62.5 percent, described it as a joint initiative of the two banks aimed at boosting competitiveness.

"This initiative is an example of a friendly consolidation...Its implementation will increase concentration of capital and strengthen the position of both banks without sacrificing their independence and identity," the ministry said in a statement.

The ministry said it planned to keep only five percent of PBR shares in reserve and would offer the remaining 24.5 percent for sale after the planned sale of PBK to a strategic investor, or a consortium next year.

Mieczyslaw Groszek, PBR's chief executive, said the move would benefit PBR by giving the institution, specialised in investment banking, access to the branch network of the large retail PBK bank, with which it would not be directly competing.
"This is a plan to become a member of a larger capital group of banks which would offer complementary products and access to a network," Groszek said.
PBK earlier this year said it wanted to form a larger financial group. It has already agreed on a cross-shareholding plan with the listed Kredyt Bank SA and signalled its interest in PBR.
Groszek said PBR was interested in taking a stake in PBK.

He also said PBK's sale would effectively conclude the privatisation of PBR, which was floated in 1995, although the treasury kept a position through its 62.5 percent holding and the 16.3 percent stake of a government-controlled agency.
"With this decision the date of the sale of PBK will also mean the conclusion of our privatisation, as the total treasury stake will fall below 50 percent," Groszek said.
